title: Infrastructure Audit and Mass Indexing Protocol
purpose: Standardized procedure for conducting comprehensive repository audits including mass file indexing, tool inventory, bug testing, and documentation generation. Ensures consistent, repeatable infrastructure assessment.

section_1_audit_scope.title: Audit Scope Definition
section_1_audit_scope.description: Define what an infrastructure audit covers and how to scope it for different repository sizes.

audit_dimensions.purpose: Map every file in the repository with type, purpose, module, and dependencies
Catalog all tools, scripts, APIs, and utilities with status and capabilities
Identify all bugs, verify previous fixes, find new issues
audit_dimensions.note: Split by subsystem: coordination, prototypes, scripts

audit_dimensions.purpose: Identify documentation gaps, create missing docs, update stale docs
Test every tool, fix broken ones, verify working ones

section_2_indexing_methodology.title: Mass File Indexing Methodology
section_2_indexing_methodology.description: How to systematically index every file in a repository.

phase_1_discovery.action: Use Glob to find all files by type

fields.module: Which system it belongs to (coordination, prototype, scripts, kb, config, etc.)
fields.has_tests: Whether test coverage exists for this file

phase_3_relationship_mapping.action: Build dependency graph showing which files depend on which others
methods: Parse Python imports to find internal dependencies
Check index.json references to discover file relationships

metrics: Files by type (Python, JSON, Markdown, etc.)
Files by module (coordination, prototype, scripts, etc.)
Test coverage percentage (files with tests / total testable files)

section_3_tool_inventory_methodology.title: Tool Inventory Methodology
section_3_tool_inventory_methodology.description: How to catalog and assess all software tools in a repository.

tool_categories.validators: Tools that check correctness (validate-storage.py, kb_validator.py, fast_validate)
tool_categories.searchers: Tools that find information (kb_search.py, fast_search, search-storage.py)
tool_categories.analyzers: Tools that evaluate quality (grade_research.py, staleness_detector.py, cross_ref_checker.py)
tool_categories.data_gatherers: Tools that collect external data (method_*.py, method_hybrid.py)
tool_categories.coordination: Tools for multi-agent operation (coordinator_hub.py, help_protocol.py, etc.)

assessment_criteria.functionality: Does the tool do what it claims? (run it and check)
assessment_criteria.reliability: Does it handle edge cases? (check error handling)
assessment_criteria.performance: Is it fast enough? (check for Go vs Python alternatives)
assessment_criteria.documentation: Is it documented? (check docstrings, README, SOP)
assessment_criteria.test_coverage: Does it have tests? (check for test_* files)
assessment_criteria.dependencies: What does it need? (check imports, requirements)
assessment_criteria.maintenance: When was it last updated? Is it actively used?

status_classification.working: Tool runs successfully, produces correct output
status_classification.broken: Tool fails with errors, produces incorrect output
status_classification.partially_functional: Tool works for some inputs but fails for others
status_classification.untested: Tool has never been verified in this session
status_classification.deprecated: Tool has been superseded by another tool

section_4_bug_audit_methodology.title: Bug Audit Methodology
section_4_bug_audit_methodology.description: How to systematically identify, verify, and track bugs across the codebase.

bug_identification_techniques.focus: Race conditions, resource leaks, missing validation, type errors
Run existing tests, check for failures
Check bugs from previous reports, verify fixes applied
Common anti-patterns: bare except, mutable defaults, unclosed files
bug_identification_techniques.effective_for: Systematic scanning for known bug patterns

bug_severity_scale.critical: Data loss, security vulnerability, system crash under normal conditions
bug_severity_scale.high: Race condition under concurrent use, incorrect results silently produced
bug_severity_scale.medium: Error handling gap, edge case failure, performance degradation
bug_severity_scale.low: Missing validation, cosmetic issue, documentation mismatch

verification_protocol.for_previously_reported_bugs: Read the source code at the reported line. Check if the fix described in the report was applied. Mark as 'verified_fixed' or 'still_present'.
verification_protocol.for_new_bugs: Provide line number, description, severity, category, and a concrete fix plan. Include code snippet showing the bug.

section_5_data_priority_rules.title: Data Priority Rules
section_5_data_priority_rules.description: When multiple sources of information exist, how to prioritize them.

priority_order.rationale: Most recent data reflects current state. Previous session outputs (bug reports, feature proposals, efficiency reports) are the most authoritative source.
Running tests reveals the actual current state. Tests passing > written claims about state.
KB entries are validated findings from prior teams. Newer entries supersede older ones on the same topic.
SOPs codify institutional knowledge. Follow SOPs unless evidence contradicts them.
Session logs provide operational context. Useful for understanding decisions but may contain outdated information.
Inline documentation is close to the code but may be stale. Trust code behavior over comments.

section_5_data_priority_rules.conflict_resolution: When two sources disagree, trust the higher-ranked source. When same-ranked sources disagree, trust the newer one. Always note the conflict in your report.

audit_team_template.small_audit: 2 teams, 4-6 agents: 1 indexing/inventory team, 1 bug testing team
audit_team_template.medium_audit: 4 teams, 8-12 agents: 1 indexing, 1 inventory, 1 bug testing, 1 documentation
audit_team_template.large_audit: 6 teams, 16-20 agents: 2 indexing/inventory, 2 bug testing (split by subsystem), 2 documentation/tool assessment
